title: Date-based API versions with per-account pinning (sound)

source.note: Adapted from Stripe's description of its API versioning design.

input.objective: Let the public REST API evolve (rename fields, change response shapes) without breaking existing integrations.
constraints: Integrations must keep working for years without code changes.
The team ships API changes weekly.
input.context: Public payments API with ~50k integrations. Today any response-shape change requires a coordinated announcement and many integrations break anyway. The backend code is a single service with a serialization layer that turns internal objects into API responses.
input.proposed_solution: Introduce date-named API versions. Each account is pinned to the version current when it made its first request; clients may override per request with a header to test upgrades. Internally the code always produces the latest shape, and a chain of small 'version change' modules transforms responses (and requests) backwards, one module per breaking change, applied from newest to the account's pinned version. Each module is documented and tested; changelog entries are generated from the modules. Additive changes do not need a new version.

ground_truth.material_issue: None: a proven approach for this context.
